question: What is the main purpose of nursing research?

options.A: To lower the financial cost of operating public hospitals
options.B: To reduce the number of working hours for hospital staff
options.C: To develop knowledge for nursing practice and improve patient outcomes
options.D: To replace physicians in diagnosing complex medical conditions

explanation: Nursing research focuses on building a scientific base for nursing care so patients receive the safest and most effective interventions. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is local health research important for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Foreign textbooks are too expensive for local nursing students to buy
options.B: International organizations pay large grants exclusively to clinical nurses
options.C: Nigerian hospitals require every nurse to publish a paper before promotion
options.D: Western guidelines do not address specific local health challenges and cultural realities

explanation: You've got this! Local research matters because health issues like malaria management and maternal care need solutions tailored to our environment, rather than just copying foreign data. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is a common research duty for a bedside staff nurse?

options.A: Collecting data and identifying study participants
options.B: Funding major multi-center clinical drug trials

explanation: Bedside nurses are closest to patients, making them well-suited to spot eligible participants and gather accurate clinical data. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the main job of a Nurse Principal Investigator?

options.A: Distributing meal trays to study participants in the clinic
options.B: Cleaning and sterilizing surgical instruments after research surgeries
options.C: Designing studies, securing funding, and overseeing ethical implementation
options.D: Administering daily bed baths to patients on the surgical ward

explanation: Think of a Principal Investigator as the captain of the study—they plan the project, find financial support, and make sure everything follows ethical guidelines. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h2)

question: What are the three main pillars that make up evidence-based practice?

options.A: Patient age, family background, and disease diagnosis
options.B: Research evidence, clinical expertise, and patient values
options.C: Hospital policy, physician orders, and insurance budgets
options.D: Textbook theory, nursing tradition, and administrative rules

explanation: EBP is a balanced approach that requires combining valid research findings with the nurse's professional judgment and what matters to the patient. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h3)

question: A nurse wants to know if a new wound dressing heals ulcers faster. What is her very first step?

options.A: Ask a clear, focused clinical question about the two dressings
options.B: Write a formal research paper for an international journal
options.C: Ask the hospital management to buy the new dressing brand
options.D: Change the dressing on all patients in the ward immediately

explanation: Great clinical thinking starts by asking the right question! Before searching or applying evidence, you must first define what you are trying to find out. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of an Institutional Review Board (IRB) in research?

options.A: To provide financial grants and equipment to student researchers
options.B: To grade the academic performance of nursing postgraduate students
options.C: To market the finished research paper to private pharmaceutical companies
options.D: To protect the rights, safety, and well-being of human research subjects

explanation: An ethics committee or IRB reviews study proposals beforehand to make sure human participants will not be harmed or exploited. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which option best describes true informed consent in clinical research?

options.A: An agreement signed by the hospital manager on behalf of the patients
options.B: A verbal promise made by the researcher that no complications will occur
options.C: An ongoing, voluntary dialogue ensuring participants understand risks and rights
options.D: A quick signature obtained by a doctor right before a surgical procedure

explanation: Informed consent isn't just a one-time signature. It's a continuous conversation making sure the participant is fully aware and knows they can walk away anytime. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which of these is a major barrier to nursing research in busy hospitals?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free time during shifts
options.B: Too many available financial grants and computers
options.C: Heavy clinical workloads and staffing shortages
options.D: Strict bans on publishing local healthcare data

explanation: Spot on! When nurse-to-patient ratios are high and everyone is exhausted, it's really tough to find the energy or time for research. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why does a lack of mentorship often slow down research growth for young nurses?

options.A: Mentorship is illegal in most public Nigerian teaching hospitals
options.B: Experienced nurses prefer to keep research findings a secret
options.C: Experienced mentors charge expensive fees to teach data analysis
options.D: Young nurses miss out on guidance, confidence building, and practical support

explanation: Having a senior colleague to show you the ropes makes all the difference. Without guidance, new researchers often feel overwhelmed and give up. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a nursing journal club in a hospital?

options.A: To raise money for the hospital's annual end-of-year party
options.B: To review and discuss recent research articles in a supportive setting
options.C: To punish nurses who make medication errors on the ward
options.D: To sell textbooks and medical equipment to patients

explanation: Journal clubs are fun and supportive! They help nurses build confidence in reading and discussing research papers together. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following does NOT help build a strong research culture?

options.A: Discouraging nurses from reading studies done by other healthcare professions
options.B: Creating mentorship programs between senior and junior staff
options.C: Establishing local grants to fund small nursing projects
options.D: Providing protected time during work hours for research activities

explanation: Healthcare is team-based! Shutting out studies from other professions hurts teamwork and slows down evidence-based practice. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h6)
